subject: A confession about what I got wrong with Predictify
preview_text: I wasn't going to send this email. But after seeing the data, I had to tell you the truth about one feature.
body_paragraphs: I don't usually write emails like this. It feels too raw. But I was looking at the user data this morning, and something hit me hard. I realized I built one part of this app completely backwards.

For months, I thought the 'Confidence Score' was the star. The big number telling you how sure the AI was. But the data doesn't lie. The users who consistently win aren't just looking at that score. They're doing one simple thing first, and 90% of people are missing it. I designed it wrong. I made it seem secondary.

That thing is the 'Deep Racecard' breakdown. Not just glancing at it, but actually opening it before you even look at the AI's pick. It shows you *why* the AI is confident. The jockey's form on wet tracks, the horse's distance proficiency, the trainer's secret weapon. It turns a guess into a calculated decision. The winners use it as their compass, not their confirmation.

Open the app right now. Before you look at today's predictions, tap into the Deep Racecard for any race. Read the 'Why This Pick' breakdown. See the machinery behind the magic. Just for one race. Then tell me if it doesn't change how you see every tip. P.S. The users who do this have a 73% higher win rate. Don't be part of the 90% who skip it.
